7.	X, a young occupational therapist from the Bay Area, arrived in Central Africa in 1967 to study mountain Ys — the world's largest living members of our biological order, of which fewer than 500 remained in the wild. She established a research camp at 3,000 meters in the volcanic Virunga Mountains and spent 18 years habituating Y families to human presence and made groundbreaking discoveries that these animals had distinct personalities, complex social structures, and deep emotional bonds. She waged an increasingly dangerous war against poachers targeting the Ys, including torturing some of them and kidnapping their children. On December 26, 1985, X was found murdered in her cabin. Her bestselling book _Ys in the Mist_ and its film adaptation starring Sigourney Weaver made her a global icon of conservation. Today the mountain Y population has grown to over 1,000 — a rare conservation success story, all the more remarkable because their habitat lies in one of the most conflict-torn regions on earth.
